answers.answer: Use planning instrumentation with RuleInstrumentationOptions::phase_only() and pass the resulting SessionState to the context: instrument_rules_with_info_spans!(options: RuleInstrumentationOptions::phase_only(), state: state). This yields phase timing without per-rule spans; full() remains available if attribution is later needed. The phases are analyzer, logical optimizer, and physical optimizer, with physical-plan creation automatically wrapped too. Evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/rule_options.rs:104-114, rule_instrumentation_macros.rs:20-27, and rule_instrumentation.rs:948-990. Probe S007 confirms the full-versus-phase-only Rule-span difference, not numerical timing accuracy. Read durations from completed spans; logical optimization may have multiple passes, and nested physical-plan creation should not be summed with its children. For total wall time including work outside those phases, add an application span around the complete planning future. No retained probe establishes that these phase spans cover SQL parsing or all application planning work.
unknowns: No numerical phase-duration or complete SQL-planning coverage probe is retained.
Caller must define whether total includes parsing, application work, and nested phases.

answers.answer: Switch to RuleInstrumentationOptions::full().with_plan_diff() through instrument_rules_with_info_spans!. Full mode creates a Rule span for each rule; when its formatted plan changes, the implementation updates otel.name to '<rule> (modified)', records datafusion.plan_diff when enabled, and adds the rule name to the enclosing phase's datafusion.effective_rules. Evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/rule_instrumentation.rs:599-627 and 200-215; rule_instrumentation_macros.rs:60-84 declares those fields. full() alone still identifies detected modifications; with_plan_diff() adds the before/after textual evidence. Detection is observational: for physical rules it first requires a different Arc, then a changed formatted plan (lines 889-917), so it is not proof of arbitrary semantic equivalence or difference. Probe S007 confirms Rule-span presence only. The integration tests disable plan diffs for nondeterministic output (tests/integration_tests.rs:229), and no retained probe confirms every modification-detection branch.
unknowns: Textual change detection is not an engineering or semantic validity judgment.
No executed retained plan-diff discrimination probe is identified.

answers.answer: Compose the planning macro with the completed session configuration: let state = instrument_rules_with_info_spans!(options: RuleInstrumentationOptions::full(), state: state); then construct SessionContext from that returned state. full() enables analyzer, logical-optimizer, and physical-optimizer Phase and Rule spans. Use phase_only() if all phases are needed but per-rule detail is unnecessary. Physical instrumentation also wraps the existing query planner and emits create_physical_plan; it preserves a custom planner by delegation. Evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/rule_options.rs:95-114, rule_instrumentation.rs:948-990, and planner.rs:62-104. Probe S007 confirms that full adds Rule spans, while S008 distinguishes physical-only selection. Admit the caller's macro target and the planner's datafusion_tracing::planner target in filters. These options do not independently add execution-node or object-store spans, and an absent/empty rule list or unexecuted phase does not promise an observed span.

answers.answer: Use the reachable builder: RuleInstrumentationOptions::builder().physical_optimizer().build(), supplied to instrument_rules_with_info_spans!(options: options, state: state). The default builder disables all phases, so this selects physical-optimizer Phase and Rule spans without analyzer or logical-optimizer instrumentation. If only coarse duration matters, physical_optimizer_phase_only() is the narrower alternative. These methods are reachable through RuleInstrumentationOptions::builder() although their builder type is not publicly nameable; content/catalogs/options.md documents the route and rule_options.rs:180-199 implements it. Probe S008 confirms the physical-only construction differs from full(). One important composition detail: physical selection also automatically wraps query-plan creation (rule_instrumentation.rs:986-990), so 'only physical optimization' does not literally mean the trace has no create_physical_plan span. That extra span uses the planner module's target; filters can distinguish it. No retained probe establishes strict exclusion under every custom planner or rule registration sequence.

answers.answer: Construct the supported execution rule with instrument_with_info_spans!(options: InstrumentationOptions::default()) and append it after the actual physical optimizer rules: builder.with_physical_optimizer_rule(custom_rule).with_physical_optimizer_rule(instrument_rule). The rule traverses the plan it receives with transform_down, wraps each uninstrumented node, and avoids wrapping an existing InstrumentedExec twice. Evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/exec_instrument_rule.rs:64-85 and content/corpus/docs/README.md:164-187. Registering it last is what makes the observed plan the final optimized one and keeps subsequent optimizers from encountering instrumentation wrappers. Probe S001 confirms node spans versus a bare control, but does not establish complete coverage of an arbitrary consumer's pipeline. Execution still has to occur under an enabled subscriber; configuration alone produces no execution evidence. InstrumentedExec is internal, so use the macro-generated optimizer rule and normal ExecutionPlan introspection rather than constructing the wrapper directly.
unknowns: S001 proves node-span presence, not complete arbitrary-plan coverage.
Consumer rule ordering and later rewrites must be inspected.

answers.answer: Move the instrumentation rule after that rewrite in the effective optimizer chain. A rule created by instrument_with_info_spans! wraps the plan available when it runs; a later rewrite can introduce nodes without instrumentation, even when the program still compiles and produces some spans. The decisive guidance is content/corpus/docs/README.md:164-184; the traversal is exec_instrument_rule.rs:64-85. Existing wrapper methods can preserve instrumentation when they rebuild their own inner plans, and README.md:189 describes that behavior, but this does not establish coverage for arbitrary nodes a later optimizer creates. Prefer builder.with_physical_optimizer_rule(rewrite).with_physical_optimizer_rule(instrument_rule). If registration order cannot be controlled, report final-plan coverage as unverified rather than treating observed spans as completeness. Probe S001 only compares an instrumented query to a bare query; no retained probe specifically tests this later-rewrite case. answers.answer: A positive preview_limit works without a custom preview_fn in the frozen source: InstrumentationOptions::builder().preview_limit(5).build() is sufficient configuration. InstrumentedExec creates a PreviewRecorder whenever the limit is greater than zero (content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/instrumented_exec.rs:154-160). PreviewRecorderBuilder::preview_fn(None) explicitly chooses default_preview_fn, which uses pretty_format_batches (preview.rs:167-200). Formatting happens when the recorder drops, after preview rows have been gathered; empty observed input or a formatting failure can still leave no preview field. This directly contradicts content/seams/preview.md and topics/00-map.md, which say no formatter means no readable preview. I follow the concrete implementation, also documented in exec_instrument_macros.rs:30-34. S002 confirms zero-limit suppression versus a preview-enabled control, but does not isolate the default-formatter case. The default fallback is therefore source-backed here, not independently re-executed or promoted to a new confirmed probe.
unknowns: Frozen summary guidance contradicts its source on the default formatter.
No retained discriminating default-versus-custom formatter probe was executed here.

answers.answer: Keep the positive limit and replace the default renderer with an Arc-wrapped Send + Sync closure: InstrumentationOptions::builder().preview_limit(5).preview_fn(Arc::new(|batch| pretty_format_compact_batch(batch, 64, 3, 10).map(|table| table.to_string()))).build(). The callback accepts &RecordBatch and returns Result<String, ArrowError>; it changes rendering rather than the sampling limit. Evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/options.rs:89-97, preview.rs:36 and 190-202, and examples/integration-utils/src/lib.rs:207-219. At recorder drop, gathered rows are sliced to the configured limit and the callback runs; errors generate a warning instead of a preview field (preview.rs:46-76). S005 confirms the compact formatter's characteristic header in its pinned construction. A zero limit still disables capture even with this callback, as S002 demonstrates. Unlike the summary's claim, a custom renderer is optional; the default fallback exists in preview.rs:167-200.
unknowns: The exact rendered width/content depends on the input schema and callback.
S005 does not establish arbitrary callback correctness or performance.

answers.answer: With one successfully polled batch in one partition, preview_limit(L) stores a slice of at most min(L, batch.num_rows()) rows while returning the original batch to the caller unchanged. It is observation, not a query-result limit. Use the execution rule with a positive limit and either the built-in formatter or a custom callback, then release the stream so its preview transfers to the recorder. content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/preview.rs:111-138 shows bounded storage and forwarding; lines 142-156 publish the accumulated partition preview on stream drop; lines 46-76 format on recorder drop. For a batch with fewer than L rows, the implementation does not invent missing rows. S002 confirms the zero-versus-positive preview switch, while S005 checks one compact rendering. Those probes do not establish a general single-batch completeness claim, and stream errors or an empty batch may leave less evidence than the configured maximum.
unknowns: No retained probe isolates every single-batch boundary and error condition.
A preview is bounded observed data, not evidence of complete query execution.

answers.answer: The same display limit is not restricted to one input batch. Each PreviewRecordingStream accumulates slices across successful batches until it stores L rows; dropping it publishes one combined preview for its partition. At recorder drop, partition previews are concatenated in partition-vector order and the combined result is sliced again to L rows before formatting. Exact evidence: content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/preview.rs:46-65, 111-156, and 207-214. Thus displayed rows are bounded by L per recorder group, while interim retained rows can scale with participating partitions; this is not random or globally ordered sampling. Concurrent distinct partitions can share a group; separate contexts, parents, or repeated partitions can create separate spans (instrumented_exec.rs:133-173, 536-556). The summary's 'one batch' statement is too narrow. S002/S005 cover enabling/rendering, not multi-batch or multi-partition aggregation. The retained source tests describe grouping behavior, but I have not executed them.
unknowns: No retained confirmed multi-batch/partition preview probe is listed.
Global query ordering and a query-wide preview budget are not established.

answers.answer: Fully consume all intended partition streams and then drop them before treating close-time fields as final for that execution. A typical shape is while let Some(batch) = stream.next().await { batch?; } followed by drop(stream), repeated for the intended streams. The execution wrapper forwards polls and releases recorder ownership in its pinned Drop, not in an EOF branch (content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/instrumented_exec.rs:595-608). When the last active stream in a recorder group is released, that group is removed (lines 559-578); preview and metrics recorders then finalize their fields. MetricsRecorder::drop aggregates the native metrics currently available (metrics.rs:51-63). The source regression span_closes_when_stream_finishes_not_when_plan_drops at lines 802-846 demonstrates the intended retained-plan lifecycle, but is source evidence, not a freshly executed probe. S003 only confirms the metrics option switch. Backend export still depends on later provider processing and shutdown.
unknowns: EOF while retaining the stream is not the same lifecycle event as dropping it.
Source regression tests were inspected but not run in this evaluation.

answers.answer: Reading one item and dropping the streams still triggers recorder cleanup and may close execution spans, but the resulting evidence describes partial consumption. Sketch: let first = stream.next().await; drop(stream); handle first explicitly. PreviewRecordingStream only accumulates successfully polled batches (content/corpus/source/datafusion-tracing/preview.rs:111-138), publishes whatever it captured on drop (142-156), and formats when its recorder is released (46-76). MetricsRecorder similarly reads native metrics at drop (metrics.rs:51-63); those numbers are not automatically full-query totals, and upstream operators may have done more work than the single output item reveals. ExecutionRecorders releases the final group when its active stream count reaches zero (instrumented_exec.rs:559-578). A closed span is therefore not a success or exhaustion certificate. The frozen S002/S003 probes cover option switches, not early cancellation; no retained confirmed partial-consumption probe establishes exact row counts or cancellation propagation.
unknowns: Exact work performed upstream before early drop is DataFusion/operator dependent.
No retained confirmed early-drop probe establishes cancellation or metric totals.

answers.answer: Retaining an Arc to the plan after execution need not keep its finished execution spans open.
